title: Module Bundler
body:
A build tool — Webpack, Vite, esbuild, Rollup — that starts from an entry file, follows every `import`/`require` to build a dependency graph, and emits a small number of bundled files for the browser to load. It stitches dozens of separate scene files into one continuous performance.

Historically the motivation was that browsers had no module system and each `<script>` cost a request; today it's more about the transformation pipeline the bundler drives: [[Transpiling]], [[Minification]], [[Tree Shaking]], [[Code Splitting]], asset hashing, and [[Source Maps]]. The critical point for interviews is that all of this runs on a **build machine** — your dev machine or a CI server — and never in the end user's browser. The browser only ever sees the finished output. Compare the [[CommonJS Module]] system used server-side in [[Node.js]].
